# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18; `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)`
  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are here too: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of `ReelCore.swift`'s
  `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-two op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eight names) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror
  of spec §5.2 every view draws from. READ-ONLY means never written back as
  is: the stored properties are `var`, so a writer edits a COPY
  (`var s = current(); s.blur = v`) rather than rebuilding one through the
  defaulted memberwise initialiser, which silently drops a field it does not
  spell out; `MotionProps.with(_:)` is motion's per-slot copy (#357). `CompositionPlan.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading GR1) is the plan's Swift side (spec §7.2): `PlanSegment`,
  `PlanRamp`, `PlanTrack`, `PlanInstruction` and `CompositionPlan`; `PlanSpeedRamp.source` is
  its `map` as a `SourceMap`, checked once at decode and not a coding key (SR-20 (c)). `ShapeProps.swift` (a pure
  move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading L3) holds the shape group: `StrokeProps`,
  `GradientStop`, `Gradient` and `ShapeProps`. `GradeProps.swift` holds `ColorAdjust` (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) beside grading's other value types. `ActionSnapshot.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, B87) holds `ActionPatch`, `ActionSnapshot` and `ActionGraphicPatch` — an
  end's `graphic.props` and `kinds`, whose `dictionary` sends `props` only. `MediaSnapshot` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`) carries a copy's or an ffmpeg conversion's `original`, and its `name` is

  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.

  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil

  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.

     2	
     3	/// The video pump of a row a bundled encoder writes (`settings.writer`, spec §11 CX-12,
     4	/// CX-15, CX-16, CX-17): the composed frames converted to I010 (I420 for `vp9_webm`'s SDR
     5	/// picture) on the export's video queue and encoded on a serial encode queue of its own — by
     6	/// SVT-AV1 for `svt_av1`, by libvpx's VP9 for `libvpx` (`ExportVideoEncoder`) — whose packets
     7	/// go to an `ExportPacketSink`: the `av1` row's passthrough `AVAssetWriterInput` as `av01`
     8	/// samples, or the WebM rows' core writer.
     9	///
    10	/// **`vp9_alpha_webm`** (CX-17 (2)–(4)): each frame is straightened in place first (G-35's
    11	/// float pass, `ExportStraightAlpha.straighten`), converted with its alpha as a second 8-bit
    12	/// picture, and encoded by `VP9AlphaEncoder`'s two libvpx streams, whose packets carry their
    13	/// alpha into the WebM.
    14	///
    15	/// **Two queues, one owner each.** The video queue reads, converts and hands each frame on,
    16	/// bounded to three in flight (`slots`) so a slow encoder holds the read back; the encode
    17	/// queue owns the encoder and the sink — every `send`, every packet, every append, the
    18	/// flush and the sink's `finish`. Progress is counted by frames SUBMITTED (the encoder's lag
    19	/// is under a second); a cancel is the writer's flag, read before each read, each send and
    20	/// each wait in the sink.
    21	///
    22	/// **The finish** runs once on the encode queue, after every frame queued before it: at the
    23	/// end of a clean read, the end of stream and a drain to the last packet; on a stop (a
    24	/// cancel, a failed read, another pump's failure), the end of stream and a drain that
    25	/// discards; after an encoder error, neither. Every exit finishes the sink and leaves the
    26	/// group exactly once. The encoder itself is torn down by `close()`, after the writer's
    27	/// pumps have all left, as the reader is (G-17).
    28	final class ExportEncodePump {
    29	    /// The settings' `writer` values this pump serves: SVT-AV1 (the AV1 rows) and libvpx
    30	    /// (`vp9_webm`, CX-16).
    31	    static let av1Writer = "svt_av1"
    32	    static let vp9Writer = "libvpx"
    33	
    34	    /// The `av01` description the MP4 sink's samples carry; nil on libvpx, which has no MP4
    35	    /// row (CX-1).
    36	    let formatDescription: CMVideoFormatDescription?
    37	    /// The WebM layout's video track (`ExportWebMLayout`): `V_AV1` with the `av1C` record and
    38	    /// the sequence header's colour at 10 bits, or `V_VP9` with no CodecPrivate, the picture's
    39	    /// CICP and its depth (CX-16 (4), (5)).
    40	    let webmCodec: ExportWebMLayout.VideoCodec
    41	    /// The picture the frames are.
    42	    let picture: ExportAV1Picture
    43	    /// True on `vp9_alpha_webm`: each frame is straightened before it is converted.
    44	    private let straightens: Bool
    45	
    46	    private var encoder: (any ExportVideoEncoder)?
    47	    /// The encoder's name, for a sentence after it is torn down.
    48	    private let encoderName: String
    49	    private let converter: ExportI010Converter
    50	    private let encodeQueue = DispatchQueue(
    51	        label: "com.kgalligan.framejob.export.encode", qos: .userInitiated)
    52	    private let range: CMTimeRange
    53	    private let frameDuration: CMTime
    54	    private let slots = DispatchSemaphore(value: 3)
    55	
    56	    // The encode queue's own state.
    57	    private var times: [Int64: CMTime] = [:]
    58	    private var lastTime = CMTime.negativeInfinity
    59	    private var encoderFailed = false
    60	    private var finished = false
    61	
    62	    init(settings: ExportSettings, canvas: CGSize, range: CMTimeRange) throws {
    63	        let frame = ExportWriter.encodedSize(settings)
    64	        let rate = settings.videoBitrate.map { max(1, $0) }
    65	            ?? ExportWriter.defaultVideoBitrate(settings, bitsPerPixel: 0.07)
    66	        let picture = ExportAV1Picture(color: settings.color)
    67	        let encoder: any ExportVideoEncoder
    68	        let bitDepth: Int
    69	        let alpha = settings.writer == Self.vp9Writer && settings.alpha
    70	        straightens = alpha
    71	        if alpha {
    72	            // CX-17: always 8-bit SDR, BT.709; the cap is the picture's alone.
    73	            bitDepth = 8
    74	            encoder = try VP9AlphaEncoder.make(
    75	                width: frame.width, height: frame.height, fps: settings.fps,
    76	                bitsPerSecond: rate)
    77	            let cicp = ExportAV1Picture.sdr.cicp
    78	            webmCodec = ExportWebMLayout.VideoCodec(
    79	                codecId: "V_VP9", codecPrivate: nil, primaries: cicp.primaries,
    80	                transfer: cicp.transfer, matrix: cicp.matrix, bitsPerChannel: 8,
    81	                alphaMode: true)
    82	            formatDescription = nil
    83	        } else if settings.writer == Self.vp9Writer {
    84	            bitDepth = VP9Encoder.bitDepth(for: picture)
    85	            encoder = try VP9Encoder(
    86	                width: frame.width, height: frame.height, fps: settings.fps,
    87	                bitsPerSecond: rate, picture: picture)
    88	            let cicp = picture.cicp
    89	            webmCodec = ExportWebMLayout.VideoCodec(
    90	                codecId: "V_VP9", codecPrivate: nil, primaries: cicp.primaries,
    91	                transfer: cicp.transfer, matrix: cicp.matrix, bitsPerChannel: bitDepth)
    92	            formatDescription = nil
    93	        } else {
    94	            bitDepth = 10
    95	            let svt = try SVTAV1Encoder(
    96	                width: frame.width, height: frame.height, fps: settings.fps,
    97	                bitsPerSecond: rate, speed: settings.encoderSpeed ?? .balanced, picture: picture)
    98	            let config: ReelAV1.Config
    99	            do {
   100	                config = try ReelAV1.config(sequenceHeader: svt.sequenceHeader)
   101	            } catch {
   102	                throw Exporter.ExportError.failed(
   103	                    "SVT-AV1's sequence header could not be read: \(error.localizedDescription)")
   104	            }
   105	            encoder = svt
   106	            webmCodec = ExportWebMLayout.VideoCodec(
   107	                codecId: "V_AV1", codecPrivate: config.record, primaries: config.color.primaries,
   108	                transfer: config.color.transfer, matrix: config.color.matrix, bitsPerChannel: 10)
   109	            formatDescription = try ExportAV1Track.formatDescription(
   110	                width: frame.width, height: frame.height, config: config, picture: picture)
   111	        }
   112	        converter = try ExportI010Converter(
   113	            width: frame.width, height: frame.height, canvas: canvas,
   114	            fills: ExportWriter.fillsTheBox(settings, canvas: canvas), picture: picture,
   115	            bitDepth: bitDepth, alpha: alpha, pool: 3)
   116	        self.encoder = encoder
   117	        encoderName = encoder.name
   118	        self.picture = picture
   119	        self.range = range
   120	        self.frameDuration = CompositionBuilder.frameDuration(settings.fps)
   121	    }
   122	
   123	    @available(*, unavailable) required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
   124	        fatalError("ExportEncodePump does not support NSCoder")
   125	    }
   126	
   127	    /// Reads `output` to its end on `queue` and encodes it into `sink`; `group` is left once
   128	    /// the sink is finished. `readFailure` answers the reader's error when the read failed;
   129	    /// `fail` records the first failure; `advance` is each submitted frame's file time.
   130	    func run(
   131	        sink: any ExportPacketSink, output: AVAssetReaderOutput, on queue: DispatchQueue,
   132	        group: DispatchGroup, isStopping: @escaping () -> Bool,
   133	        readFailure: @escaping () -> (any Error)?, fail: @escaping (any Error) -> Void,
   134	        advance: @escaping (CMTime) -> Void
   135	    ) {
   136	        group.enter()
   137	        let finish: (Bool) -> Void = { [self] clean in
   138	            encodeQueue.async {
   139	                self.finish(
   140	                    clean: clean, sink: sink, group: group, isStopping: isStopping, fail: fail)
   141	            }
   142	        }
   143	        queue.async { [self] in
   144	            var index: Int64 = 0
   145	            while true {
   146	                guard !isStopping() else { return finish(false) }
   147	                guard let sample = output.copyNextSampleBuffer() else {
   148	                    // Dry: the range is read, or the read failed — never a branded, done
   149	                    // file after a failed read.
   150	                    if let error = readFailure() {
   151	                        fail(error)
   152	                        return finish(false)
   153	                    }
   154	                    return finish(true)
   155	                }
   156	                let time = CMSampleBufferGetPresentationTimeStamp(sample) - range.start
   157	                guard time.isNumeric, time >= .zero else { continue }
   158	                slots.wait()
   159	                guard let pixels = CMSampleBufferGetImageBuffer(sample) else {
   160	                    slots.signal()
   161	                    fail(Exporter.ExportError.failed(
   162	                        "A frame could not be prepared for the encoder."))
   163	                    return finish(false)
   164	                }
   165	                // G-35's straight alpha (CX-17 (2)), in place on the reader's own copy.
   166	                guard !straightens || ExportStraightAlpha.straighten(pixels) else {
   167	                    slots.signal()
   168	                    fail(Exporter.ExportError.failed(
   169	                        "A frame's transparency could not be written straight."))
   170	                    return finish(false)
   171	                }
   172	                guard let frame = converter.convert(pixels) else {
   173	                    slots.signal()
   174	                    fail(Exporter.ExportError.failed(
   175	                        "A frame could not be prepared for the encoder."))
   176	                    return finish(false)
   177	                }
   178	                let at = index
   179	                index += 1
   180	                encodeQueue.async {
   181	                    self.encode(
   182	                        frame, index: at, time: time, sink: sink, isStopping: isStopping,
   183	                        fail: fail)
   184	                }
   185	                advance(time)
   186	            }
   187	        }
   188	    }
   189	
   190	    /// The encoder's teardown, on the encode queue, once every input is finished.
   191	    func close() {
   192	        encodeQueue.async { [self] in encoder = nil }
   193	    }
   194	
   195	    // MARK: - The encode queue
   196	
   197	    private func encode(
   198	        _ frame: I010Frame, index: Int64, time: CMTime, sink: any ExportPacketSink,
   199	        isStopping: () -> Bool, fail: (any Error) -> Void
   200	    ) {
   201	        defer {
   202	            converter.recycle(frame)
   203	            slots.signal()
   204	        }
   205	        guard !finished, !encoderFailed, !isStopping(), let encoder else { return }
   206	        do {
   207	            try encoder.send(frame, index: index)
   208	            times[index] = time
   209	            while let packet = try encoder.nextPacket(wait: false) {
   210	                guard write(packet, sink: sink, isStopping: isStopping, fail: fail) else {
   211	                    return
   212	                }
   213	            }
   214	        } catch {
   215	            encoderFailed = true
   216	            fail(error)
   217	        }
   218	    }
   219	
   220	    /// One packet into the file: false once the export cannot go on.
   221	    private func write(
   222	        _ packet: ExportEncodedPacket, sink: any ExportPacketSink, isStopping: () -> Bool,
   223	        fail: (any Error) -> Void
   224	    ) -> Bool {
   225	        guard !packet.data.isEmpty else { return true }
   226	        let data: Data
   227	        do {
   228	            data = try encoder?.containerBytes(packet.data) ?? packet.data
   229	        } catch {
   230	            fail(error)
   231	            return false
   232	        }
   233	        guard let time = times.removeValue(forKey: packet.pts), time > lastTime else {
   234	            fail(Exporter.ExportError.failed("\(encoderName) wrote a frame out of order."))
   235	            return false
   236	        }
   237	        lastTime = time
   238	        if let error = sink.append(
   239	            data, alpha: packet.alpha, at: time, duration: frameDuration, key: packet.isKey,
   240	            isStopping: isStopping)
   241	        {
   242	            if !(error is ExportPacketSinkStopped) { fail(error) }
   243	            return false
   244	        }
   245	        return true
   246	    }
   247	
   248	    /// The one exit: the end of stream and the drain as `clean` and the encoder allow, then
   249	    /// the sink finished and the group left, exactly once.
   250	    private func finish(
   251	        clean: Bool, sink: any ExportPacketSink, group: DispatchGroup, isStopping: () -> Bool,
   252	        fail: (any Error) -> Void
   253	    ) {
   254	        guard !finished else { return }
   255	        finished = true
   256	        defer {
   257	            sink.finish()
   258	            group.leave()
   259	        }
   260	        guard !encoderFailed, let encoder else { return }
   261	        do {
   262	            try encoder.sendEndOfStream()
   263	            var writing = clean && !isStopping()
   264	            while let packet = try encoder.nextPacket(wait: true) {
   265	                if writing {
   266	                    writing = write(packet, sink: sink, isStopping: isStopping, fail: fail)
   267	                }
   268	                if packet.isLast { break }
   269	            }
   270	        } catch {
   271	            encoderFailed = true
   272	            if clean { fail(error) }
   273	        }
   274	    }
   275	}

   277	                readFailure: { [weak self] in self?.readFailure(of: self?.videoReader) },
   278	                fail: { [weak self] error in self?.stopped(with: error) },
   279	                advance: { [weak self] time in self?.advance(to: time) })
   280	            // The video reader's own cancel, on its queue after the pump's read loop (#378).
   281	            group.enter()
   282	            videoQueue.async { [weak self] in
   283	                defer { group.leave() }
   284	                if let self, self.isStopping { self.videoReader?.cancelReading() }
   285	            }
   286	        } else if let input = videoInput, let output = videoOutput, let videoReader {
   287	            pump(
   288	                input, from: output, reading: videoReader, on: videoQueue, group: group,
   289	                tracksProgress: true, frames: frames)
   290	        }

   292	            // Audio drives the bar only when there is no picture to drive it,
   293	            // and it is the only pump that can carry a gain.
   294	            pump(
   295	                input, from: output, reading: audioReader, on: audioQueue, group: group,
   296	                tracksProgress: videoInput == nil, gain: audioGain, end: audioEnd)
   297	        }

   299	            pumpChapters(input, on: chapterQueue, group: group)
   300	        }
   301	        group.notify(queue: .main) { [weak self] in self?.allInputsFinished() }
   302	    }
   303	
   304	    /// Stops as soon as the pumps notice — within one sample. Safe from any
   305	    /// thread and safe to call twice. It ONLY sets the flag: each pump cancels
   306	    /// its own reader on its own queue after its own last read, and the writer
   307	    /// is cancelled in `allInputsFinished`, after every pump has left its loop
   308	    /// (spec §11 #378).
   309	    ///
   310	    /// **Cancelling the reader from here crashed the app** (road map 10
   311	    /// §10.6, G3c). `reader.cancelReading()` on main while a pump was inside
   312	    /// `copyNextSampleBuffer` tore the reader down under it: EXC_BREAKPOINT
   313	    /// in `CMVideoFormatDescriptionMatchesImageBuffer` on the video queue, in
   314	    /// 12 of 30 mid-export cancels of a 4K graphic project — the sheet's and
   315	    /// the queue's Cancel path — and 16 of 40 exports stopped by a failing
   316	    /// graphic. The cost is that a pump blocked on a slow read finishes that
   317	    /// one sample before it stops. A pump can no longer be starved by the
   318	    /// other's stop, each output having its own reader (#378); a
   319	    /// `copyNextSampleBuffer` that never returns for another reason (a volume
   320	    /// that stops answering) is not woken, and accepted (spec §11 G-17). A
   321	    /// cancel before `start` is refused there; `cancelReading()` before
   322	    /// `startReading()` would raise.
   323	    func cancel() {
   324	        lock.lock()
   325	        cancelRequested = true
   326	        lock.unlock()
   327	    }
   328	
   329	    /// 0…1, from the last sample appended. `AVAssetWriter` has no progress of
   330	    /// its own, so this is it.
   331	    var progress: Double {
   332	        lock.lock()
   333	        defer { lock.unlock() }
   334	        return progressValue
   335	    }

   337	    // MARK: - The pumps

   339	    /// Moves one output's samples into one input until the output runs dry,
   340	    /// the write fails, or the export is cancelled.
   341	    ///
   342	    /// `requestMediaDataWhenReady` re-enters this block whenever the encoder
   343	    /// has room, so the "have I already finished?" flag lives outside it and
   344	    /// is only ever touched on `queue`, which is serial.
   345	    ///

   347	    /// one too unless the export asked to be normalised — which is what
   348	    /// keeps an ordinary export on exactly the samples it had before.
   349	    /// `frames` is non-nil only for the video pump of a row `frameForm`
   350	    /// names: each frame is then converted by it (`ExportFrames`). `reader` is
   351	    /// the output's own, which `stop` cancels after the last read when the
   352	    /// write is stopping (#378). `-RCDevExportFault` reaches the audio pump
   353	    /// before a read and the video pump before an append.
   354	    private func pump(
   355	        _ input: AVAssetWriterInput, from output: AVAssetReaderOutput,
   356	        reading reader: AVAssetReader, on queue: DispatchQueue, group: DispatchGroup,
   357	        tracksProgress: Bool, gain: ExportAudioGain? = nil, frames: ExportFrames? = nil,
   358	        end: ExportAudioEnd? = nil
   359	    ) {
   360	        group.enter()
   361	        var finished = false
   362	        var reads = 0
   363	        var appends = 0
   364	        let stop: () -> Void = { [weak self] in
   365	            guard !finished else { return }
   366	            finished = true
   367	            // Its own reader, on its own queue, after its own last read (G-17).
   368	            if self?.isStopping ?? true { reader.cancelReading() }
   369	            input.markAsFinished()
   370	            group.leave()
   371	        }
   372	        input.requestMediaDataWhenReady(on: queue) { [weak self] in
   373	            guard let self = self else { return }
   374	            while input.isReadyForMoreMediaData {
   375	                guard !finished else { return }
   376	                guard !self.isStopping else {
   377	                    stop()
   378	                    return
   379	                }
   380	                if end != nil, end?.isPadding != true {
   381	                    reads += 1
   382	                    do { try self.fault?.beforeAudioRead(reads) } catch {
   383	                        self.stopped(with: error)
   384	                        stop()
   385	                        return
   386	                    }
   387	                }
   388	                guard let decoded = end?.isPadding == true ? nil : output.copyNextSampleBuffer()

   390	                    // Dry: the range is written, or the read failed — and only
   391	                    // the last is ours to name.
   392	                    if let error = self.readFailure(of: reader) {
   393	                        self.stopped(with: error)
   394	                    } else if let end = end, !self.isStopping {

   396	                        guard let padded = end.pad(input) else { return }
   397	                        if !padded {
   398	                            self.stopped(with: self.writer.error
   399	                                ?? Exporter.ExportError.failed("The file could not be written."))
   400	                        }
   401	                    }
   402	                    stop()
   403	                    return
   404	                }
   405	                let time = CMSampleBufferGetPresentationTimeStamp(decoded) - self.range.start
   406	                // A sample that starts before the range does not belong to
   407	                // this file. The reader clips to `timeRange`, so this is a
   408	                // boundary frame, not a common case.
   409	                guard time.isNumeric, time >= .zero else { continue }
   410	                // An empty buffer has nothing to gain and is not malformed:
   411	                // it is skipped, as the old Int16 kernel passed it through.
   412	                if gain != nil, CMSampleBufferGetNumSamples(decoded) == 0 { continue }
   413	                // The gain makes a NEW 16-bit buffer from the float one,
   414	                // before `retimed`; with no gain the decode goes on as read.
   415	                guard let sample = gain == nil ? decoded : gain?.apply(to: decoded) else {
   416	                    self.stopped(
   417	                        with: Exporter.ExportError.failed(
   418	                            "The loudness gain could not be applied to a sample."))
   419	                    stop()
   420	                    return
   421	                }
   422	                // A `frameForm` row's frame, converted (spec §11 G-35, PR-3),
   423	                // before `retimed`; any other goes on as read.
   424	                guard let ready = frames == nil ? sample : frames?.convert(sample) else {
   425	                    self.stopped(
   426	                        with: Exporter.ExportError.failed(
   427	                            frames?.failure ?? "A frame could not be prepared for the encoder."))
   428	                    stop()
   429	                    return
   430	                }
   431	                guard let rebased = Self.retimed(ready, by: self.range.start) else {
   432	                    self.stopped(
   433	                        with: Exporter.ExportError.failed(
   434	                            "A sample could not be re-timed for the file."))
   435	                    stop()
   436	                    return
   437	                }
   438	                // A buffer past the range's end is cut or dropped (#337).
   439	                guard let fitted = end == nil ? rebased : end?.fit(rebased) else { continue }
   440	                if end == nil {
   441	                    appends += 1
   442	                    if let error = self.fault?.videoPacket(appends) {
   443	                        self.stopped(with: error)
   444	                        stop()
   445	                        return
   446	                    }
   447	                }
   448	                guard input.append(fitted) else {
   449	                    self.stopped(
   450	                        with: self.writer.error
   451	                            ?? Exporter.ExportError.failed("The file could not be written."))
   452	                    stop()
   453	                    return
   454	                }
   455	                if tracksProgress { self.advance(to: time) }
   456	            }
   457	        }
   458	    }
   459	
   460	    // MARK: - Finishing
   461	
   462	    /// True once anything has asked the write to stop.
   463	    var isStopping: Bool {
   464	        lock.lock()
   465	        defer { lock.unlock() }
   466	        return cancelRequested || failure != nil
   467	    }
   468	
   469	    /// Records the first failure; later ones are noise from the other pumps
   470	    /// unwinding. The other pumps see it before their next sample, and each
   471	    /// reader is cancelled by its own pump (`cancel`'s doc says why).
   472	    private func stopped(with error: any Error) {
   473	        lock.lock()
   474	        if failure == nil { failure = error }
   475	        lock.unlock()
   476	    }
   477	
   478	    /// `reader`'s error once its read failed, else nil — each pump's question at
   479	    /// the end of its read.
   480	    private func readFailure(of reader: AVAssetReader?) -> (any Error)? {
   481	        guard let reader, reader.status == .failed else { return nil }
   482	        return reader.error
   483	            ?? Exporter.ExportError.failed("The composition could not be read to the end.")
   484	    }
   485	
   486	    private func advance(to time: CMTime) {
   487	        guard totalSeconds > 0 else { return }
   488	        let fraction = CMTimeGetSeconds(time) / totalSeconds
   489	        lock.lock()
   490	        progressValue = min(max(fraction, progressValue), 1)

   492	    }

   494	    /// Main thread, once every input has marked itself finished — each reader

29	/// compositor's premultiplied frame is un-premultiplied, its transparent
30	/// pixels' colour filled from the nearest visible one, and labelled
31	/// straight (`ExportStraightAlpha`, spec §11 G-35); `h264`'s, `hevc`'s and
32	/// `hevc_alpha`'s are first rounded to 8 bits (`ExportFrames`, PR-3), and
33	/// every other row's frame goes to the encoder as the compositor drew it.
34	///
35	/// **Why the read is a reader and not a second render.** The alternative —
36	/// driving the compositor by hand over an `AVAssetImageGenerator`, one frame
37	/// at a time — is a second rendering path with its own timing, and the whole
38	/// design exists so there is not one. `AVAssetReaderVideoCompositionOutput`
39	/// runs the video composition on AVFoundation's own schedule and hands back
40	/// the very buffers the compositor filled.
41	///
42	/// **Times are rebased, not mapped.** The reader's range starts at
43	/// `settings.start`; every sample is re-timed by subtracting it and the
44	/// writing session starts at zero, so an in/out export is a file that begins
45	/// at 00:00 like the session path's did. Letting `startSession(atSourceTime:)`
46	/// do the mapping instead would leave the container's edit list to decide,
47	/// which players disagree about.
48	///
49	/// **One reader per output** (spec §11 #378, CX-15 (2)): the video composition
50	/// output and the audio mix output each have an `AVAssetReader` over the same
51	/// composition and range, so neither read can be starved by the other pump's stop.
52	///
53	/// **Cancellation and progress.** Every sample checks the flag, so a cancel
54	/// lands within one frame, and each pump cancels its own reader on its own
55	/// queue after its own last read (`cancel`); `AVAssetWriter` has no `progress` of its own, so
56	/// the fraction is kept here from the presentation time of the last sample
57	/// appended and `Exporter`'s 0.1 s timer reads it.
58	final class ExportWriter {
59	
60	    /// The composition, held for the whole write. Not merely tidiness: the
61	    /// compositor asks `RecipeSource` for a recipe per frame, and the
62	    /// instructions inside this object carry the key it asks under.
63	    let built: BuiltComposition
64	    private let destination: URL
65	    /// The slice of the composition being written, in composition time.
66	    let range: CMTimeRange
67	    /// `range.duration` in seconds, or 0 for a degenerate range — the
68	    /// denominator of `progress`.
69	    private let totalSeconds: Double
70	
71	    /// The video composition's reader, nil for an audio-only row, and the mix's,
72	    /// nil for a silent movie (#378); each cancelled only by its own pump.
73	    private let videoReader: AVAssetReader?
74	    let audioReader: AVAssetReader?
75	    let writer: AVAssetWriter
76	    private var videoOutput: AVAssetReaderOutput?
77	    var videoInput: AVAssetWriterInput?
78	    var audioOutput: AVAssetReaderOutput?
79	    var audioInput: AVAssetWriterInput?
80	    var chapterInput: AVAssetWriterInput?
81	    var chapterSamples: [CMSampleBuffer] = []
82	
83	    /// One serial queue per input, as `requestMediaDataWhenReady` requires.
84	    /// Separate queues rather than one shared serial queue: the audio pump
85	    /// must not sit behind a 4K frame being appended.
86	    private let videoQueue = DispatchQueue(
87	        label: "com.kgalligan.framejob.export.video", qos: .userInitiated)
88	    private let audioQueue = DispatchQueue(
89	        label: "com.kgalligan.framejob.export.audio", qos: .userInitiated)
90	    private let chapterQueue = DispatchQueue(
91	        label: "com.kgalligan.framejob.export.chapters", qos: .userInitiated)
92	
93	    /// Guards everything the pumps and the main thread both touch.
94	    private let lock = NSLock()
95	    private var progressValue: Double = 0
96	    private var cancelRequested = false
97	    private var failure: (any Error)?
98	
99	    /// Called once, on the main thread, and then dropped.
100	    private var completion: ((Result<URL, any Error>) -> Void)?
101	
102	    /// The loudness normalisation's gain, or nil when there is none — and
103	    /// nil is not a multiply by one: the audio is then read as the 16-bit
104	    /// decode and `pump` never enters the gain path, so an export that was
105	    /// not normalised is byte-identical to one from before this file knew
106	    /// what loudness was, by construction rather than by argument.
107	    ///
108	    /// Written once, on the main thread, between `init` and `start`; read
109	    /// by `start` and then only on `audioQueue`. Not under the lock for that
110	    /// reason and no other.
111	    private(set) var audioGain: ExportAudioGain?
112	
113	    /// What the video pump makes of each frame (spec §11 G-35, PR-3;
114	    /// `frameForm`), set once by `addVideo` in `init` and read only by
115	    /// `start`; nil hands each frame on as drawn.
116	    private var frames: ExportFrames?
117	
118	    /// The encoder row's video pump (`settings.writer`, spec §11 CX-12), set by `addVideo`;
119	    /// nil on every row AVFoundation encodes.
120	    private var encodePump: ExportEncodePump?
121	
122	    /// The audio pump's `end`: the sound cut at the range, padded to it (#337).
123	    private let audioEnd: ExportAudioEnd
124	
125	    /// `-RCDevExportFault` (`ExportWebMDevFault`, dev tools only, #378), else nil.
126	    private let fault = ExportWebMDevFault.current(key: ExportWebMDevFault.writerKey)
127	
128	    /// Builds the readers, the writer and every track, or throws the
129	    /// `Exporter.ExportError` the sheet should show. Nothing is read or
130	    /// written until `start`.
131	    init(
132	        built: BuiltComposition, settings: ExportSettings, chapters: [ExportChapter], to url: URL
133	    ) throws {
134	        guard let fileType = Exporter.fileType(for: settings) else {
135	            throw Exporter.ExportError.fileTypeUnsupported(settings.container)
136	        }
137	        self.built = built
138	        self.destination = url
139	        self.range = Exporter.timeRange(settings, composition: built.composition)
140	        self.totalSeconds = max(0, CMTimeGetSeconds(range.duration))
141	        self.audioEnd = ExportAudioEnd(range: range)

143	        let hasAudio = !built.composition.tracks(withMediaType: .audio).isEmpty

154	
155	        try addVideo(settings: settings)
156	        try addAudio(settings: settings)

158	    }
159	
160	    @available(*, unavailable) required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
161	        fatalError("ExportWriter does not support NSCoder")
162	    }
163	
164	    /// Multiplies every audio sample by `gain` on the way to the encoder —
165	    /// the second half of a loudness-normalised export (`Exporter`'s
166	    /// measurement pass is the first).
167	    ///
168	    /// Main thread, after `init` and before `start`: the gain is the
169	    /// measurement's answer, and the measurement runs on the build queue
170	    /// while this object is being constructed. `Exporter.startWriting` is
171	    /// the one caller.
172	    ///
173	    /// A non-finite or non-positive gain is ignored rather than obeyed. A
174	    /// gain is a number derived from a measurement, and a measurement of
175	    /// digital silence is −∞; multiplying a file by that would be a silent
176	    /// export reported as a success. A gain of exactly 1 is ignored too, so
177	    /// it keeps the un-normalised read.
178	    func normalizeAudio(byLinearGain gain: Float) {
179	        guard gain.isFinite, gain > 0, gain != 1 else { return }
180	        audioGain = ExportAudioGain(linearGain: gain)
181	    }
182	
183	    // MARK: - Tracks
184	
185	    /// The video half: the composition's video tracks through the video
186	    /// composition, into one encoder input.
187	    ///
188	    /// An audio-only preset gets NO video at all, for the reason the session
189	    /// path gives: attaching the video composition asks the custom compositor
190	    /// to render frames nothing will write.
191	    private func addVideo(settings: ExportSettings) throws {
192	        guard !settings.isAudioOnly else { return }
193	        let tracks = built.composition.tracks(withMediaType: .video)
194	        // CompositionBuilder gives a text-and-shapes-only timeline a
195	        // placeholder track precisely so this is never empty; if it still is,
196	        // the bundled resource is missing and there is nothing to compose
197	        // against.
198	        guard !tracks.isEmpty else { throw Exporter.ExportError.emptyTimeline }
199	        let canvas = built.videoComposition.renderSize
200	        try Self.checkAlphaSurvivesTheSize(settings, canvas: canvas)
201	        let output = Self.videoReadOutput(built, settings: settings)
202	        guard videoReader!.canAdd(output) else {
203	            throw Exporter.ExportError.failed(
204	                "The composition could not be read for export.")
205	        }
206	        videoReader!.add(output)
207	
208	        // An encoder row's packets go in as they are (`ExportEncodePump`).
209	        let pump = settings.writer == ExportEncodePump.av1Writer
210	            ? try ExportEncodePump(settings: settings, canvas: canvas, range: range) : nil
211	        let input = try pump.map {
212	            AVAssetWriterInput(
213	                mediaType: .video, outputSettings: nil, sourceFormatHint: $0.formatDescription)
214	        } ?? AVAssetWriterInput(
215	            mediaType: .video, outputSettings: try Self.videoSettings(settings, canvas: canvas))
216	        input.expectsMediaDataInRealTime = false
217	        guard writer.canAdd(input) else {
218	            throw Exporter.ExportError.presetUnavailable(Self.presetName(settings))
219	        }
220	        writer.add(input)
221	        videoOutput = output
222	        videoInput = input
223	        encodePump = pump
224	        frames = Self.frameForm(settings).map { ExportFrames(form: $0) }
225	    }
226	
227	    // MARK: - Running
228	
229	    /// Starts the write. Main thread; `completion` is called exactly once, on
230	    /// the main thread, and may be called before this returns if the writer
231	    /// refuses to start at all.
232	    func start(completion: @escaping (Result<URL, any Error>) -> Void) {
233	        self.completion = completion
234	        // A cancel that arrived BEFORE this call is honoured here, before the
235	        // reader or the writer has started, rather than one sample later.
236	        lock.lock()
237	        let cancelledAlready = cancelRequested
238	        lock.unlock()
239	        guard !cancelledAlready else {
240	            report(.failure(Exporter.ExportError.cancelled))
241	            return
242	        }
243	        if audioInput != nil, !addAudioOutput() {
244	            report(.failure(Exporter.ExportError.failed(
245	                "The audio mix could not be read for export.")))
246	            return
247	        }
248	        guard writer.startWriting() else {
249	            report(.failure(writer.error ?? Exporter.ExportError.failed(
250	                "The file could not be opened for writing.")))
251	            return
252	        }
253	        if let videoReader, !videoReader.startReading() {
254	            writer.cancelWriting()
255	            report(.failure(videoReader.error ?? Exporter.ExportError.failed(
256	                "The composition could not be read for export.")))
257	            return
258	        }
259	        // A reader not yet started is started (as `ExportWebMWriter` does).
260	        if let audioReader, audioReader.status == .unknown, !audioReader.startReading() {
261	            videoReader?.cancelReading()
262	            writer.cancelWriting()
263	            report(.failure(audioReader.error ?? Exporter.ExportError.failed(
264	                "The audio mix could not be read for export.")))
265	            return
266	        }
267	        // Zero, not `range.start`: the samples are rebased on the way in, so
268	        // the file's timeline is its own.
269	        writer.startSession(atSourceTime: .zero)
270	
271	        let group = DispatchGroup()
272	        if let input = videoInput, let output = videoOutput, let encodePump {
273	            encodePump.run(
274	                sink: ExportMP4PacketSink(input: input, format: encodePump.formatDescription),
275	                output: output, on: videoQueue, group: group,
276	                isStopping: { [weak self] in self?.isStopping ?? true },
277	                readFailure: { [weak self] in self?.readFailure(of: self?.videoReader) },
278	                fail: { [weak self] error in self?.stopped(with: error) },
279	                advance: { [weak self] time in self?.advance(to: time) })
280	            // The video reader's own cancel, on its queue after the pump's read loop (#378).
281	            group.enter()
282	            videoQueue.async { [weak self] in
283	                defer { group.leave() }
284	                if let self, self.isStopping { self.videoReader?.cancelReading() }
285	            }
286	        } else if let input = videoInput, let output = videoOutput, let videoReader {
287	            pump(
288	                input, from: output, reading: videoReader, on: videoQueue, group: group,
289	                tracksProgress: true, frames: frames)
290	        }
291	        if let input = audioInput, let output = audioOutput, let audioReader {
292	            // Audio drives the bar only when there is no picture to drive it,
293	            // and it is the only pump that can carry a gain.
294	            pump(
295	                input, from: output, reading: audioReader, on: audioQueue, group: group,
296	                tracksProgress: videoInput == nil, gain: audioGain, end: audioEnd)
297	        }
298	        if let input = chapterInput {
299	            pumpChapters(input, on: chapterQueue, group: group)
300	        }
301	        group.notify(queue: .main) { [weak self] in self?.allInputsFinished() }
302	    }
303	
304	    /// Stops as soon as the pumps notice — within one sample. Safe from any
305	    /// thread and safe to call twice. It ONLY sets the flag: each pump cancels
306	    /// its own reader on its own queue after its own last read, and the writer
307	    /// is cancelled in `allInputsFinished`, after every pump has left its loop
308	    /// (spec §11 #378).
309	    ///
310	    /// **Cancelling the reader from here crashed the app** (road map 10
311	    /// §10.6, G3c). `reader.cancelReading()` on main while a pump was inside
312	    /// `copyNextSampleBuffer` tore the reader down under it: EXC_BREAKPOINT
313	    /// in `CMVideoFormatDescriptionMatchesImageBuffer` on the video queue, in
314	    /// 12 of 30 mid-export cancels of a 4K graphic project — the sheet's and
315	    /// the queue's Cancel path — and 16 of 40 exports stopped by a failing
316	    /// graphic. The cost is that a pump blocked on a slow read finishes that
317	    /// one sample before it stops. A pump can no longer be starved by the
318	    /// other's stop, each output having its own reader (#378); a
319	    /// `copyNextSampleBuffer` that never returns for another reason (a volume
320	    /// that stops answering) is not woken, and accepted (spec §11 G-17). A
321	    /// cancel before `start` is refused there; `cancelReading()` before
322	    /// `startReading()` would raise.
323	    func cancel() {
324	        lock.lock()
325	        cancelRequested = true
326	        lock.unlock()
327	    }
328	
329	    /// 0…1, from the last sample appended. `AVAssetWriter` has no progress of
330	    /// its own, so this is it.
331	    var progress: Double {
332	        lock.lock()
333	        defer { lock.unlock() }
334	        return progressValue
335	    }
336	
337	    // MARK: - The pumps
338	
339	    /// Moves one output's samples into one input until the output runs dry,
340	    /// the write fails, or the export is cancelled.
341	    ///
342	    /// `requestMediaDataWhenReady` re-enters this block whenever the encoder
343	    /// has room, so the "have I already finished?" flag lives outside it and
344	    /// is only ever touched on `queue`, which is serial.
345	    ///
346	    /// `gain` is nil for every pump but the audio one, and nil for the audio
347	    /// one too unless the export asked to be normalised — which is what
348	    /// keeps an ordinary export on exactly the samples it had before.
349	    /// `frames` is non-nil only for the video pump of a row `frameForm`
350	    /// names: each frame is then converted by it (`ExportFrames`). `reader` is
351	    /// the output's own, which `stop` cancels after the last read when the
352	    /// write is stopping (#378). `-RCDevExportFault` reaches the audio pump
353	    /// before a read and the video pump before an append.
354	    private func pump(
355	        _ input: AVAssetWriterInput, from output: AVAssetReaderOutput,
356	        reading reader: AVAssetReader, on queue: DispatchQueue, group: DispatchGroup,
357	        tracksProgress: Bool, gain: ExportAudioGain? = nil, frames: ExportFrames? = nil,
358	        end: ExportAudioEnd? = nil
359	    ) {
360	        group.enter()
361	        var finished = false
362	        var reads = 0
363	        var appends = 0
364	        let stop: () -> Void = { [weak self] in
365	            guard !finished else { return }
366	            finished = true
367	            // Its own reader, on its own queue, after its own last read (G-17).
368	            if self?.isStopping ?? true { reader.cancelReading() }
369	            input.markAsFinished()
370	            group.leave()
371	        }
372	        input.requestMediaDataWhenReady(on: queue) { [weak self] in
373	            guard let self = self else { return }
374	            while input.isReadyForMoreMediaData {
375	                guard !finished else { return }
376	                guard !self.isStopping else {
377	                    stop()
378	                    return
379	                }
380	                if end != nil, end?.isPadding != true {
381	                    reads += 1
382	                    do { try self.fault?.beforeAudioRead(reads) } catch {
383	                        self.stopped(with: error)
384	                        stop()
385	                        return
386	                    }
387	                }
388	                guard let decoded = end?.isPadding == true ? nil : output.copyNextSampleBuffer()
389	                else {
390	                    // Dry: the range is written, or the read failed — and only
391	                    // the last is ours to name.
392	                    if let error = self.readFailure(of: reader) {
393	                        self.stopped(with: error)
394	                    } else if let end = end, !self.isStopping {
395	                        // Silence up to the range's end, while the input has room (#337).
396	                        guard let padded = end.pad(input) else { return }
397	                        if !padded {
398	                            self.stopped(with: self.writer.error
399	                                ?? Exporter.ExportError.failed("The file could not be written."))
400	                        }
401	                    }
402	                    stop()
403	                    return
404	                }
405	                let time = CMSampleBufferGetPresentationTimeStamp(decoded) - self.range.start
406	                // A sample that starts before the range does not belong to
407	                // this file. The reader clips to `timeRange`, so this is a
408	                // boundary frame, not a common case.
409	                guard time.isNumeric, time >= .zero else { continue }
410	                // An empty buffer has nothing to gain and is not malformed:
411	                // it is skipped, as the old Int16 kernel passed it through.
412	                if gain != nil, CMSampleBufferGetNumSamples(decoded) == 0 { continue }
413	                // The gain makes a NEW 16-bit buffer from the float one,
414	                // before `retimed`; with no gain the decode goes on as read.
415	                guard let sample = gain == nil ? decoded : gain?.apply(to: decoded) else {
416	                    self.stopped(
417	                        with: Exporter.ExportError.failed(
418	                            "The loudness gain could not be applied to a sample."))
419	                    stop()
420	                    return
421	                }
422	                // A `frameForm` row's frame, converted (spec §11 G-35, PR-3),
423	                // before `retimed`; any other goes on as read.
424	                guard let ready = frames == nil ? sample : frames?.convert(sample) else {
425	                    self.stopped(
426	                        with: Exporter.ExportError.failed(
427	                            frames?.failure ?? "A frame could not be prepared for the encoder."))
428	                    stop()
429	                    return
430	                }
431	                guard let rebased = Self.retimed(ready, by: self.range.start) else {
432	                    self.stopped(
433	                        with: Exporter.ExportError.failed(
434	                            "A sample could not be re-timed for the file."))
435	                    stop()
436	                    return
437	                }
438	                // A buffer past the range's end is cut or dropped (#337).
439	                guard let fitted = end == nil ? rebased : end?.fit(rebased) else { continue }
440	                if end == nil {
441	                    appends += 1
442	                    if let error = self.fault?.videoPacket(appends) {
443	                        self.stopped(with: error)
444	                        stop()
445	                        return
446	                    }
447	                }
448	                guard input.append(fitted) else {
449	                    self.stopped(
450	                        with: self.writer.error
451	                            ?? Exporter.ExportError.failed("The file could not be written."))
452	                    stop()
453	                    return
454	                }
455	                if tracksProgress { self.advance(to: time) }
456	            }
457	        }
458	    }
459	
460	    // MARK: - Finishing
461	
462	    /// True once anything has asked the write to stop.
463	    var isStopping: Bool {
464	        lock.lock()
465	        defer { lock.unlock() }
466	        return cancelRequested || failure != nil
467	    }
468	
469	    /// Records the first failure; later ones are noise from the other pumps
470	    /// unwinding. The other pumps see it before their next sample, and each
471	    /// reader is cancelled by its own pump (`cancel`'s doc says why).
472	    private func stopped(with error: any Error) {
473	        lock.lock()
474	        if failure == nil { failure = error }
475	        lock.unlock()
476	    }
477	
478	    /// `reader`'s error once its read failed, else nil — each pump's question at
479	    /// the end of its read.
480	    private func readFailure(of reader: AVAssetReader?) -> (any Error)? {
481	        guard let reader, reader.status == .failed else { return nil }
482	        return reader.error
483	            ?? Exporter.ExportError.failed("The composition could not be read to the end.")
484	    }
485	
486	    private func advance(to time: CMTime) {
487	        guard totalSeconds > 0 else { return }
488	        let fraction = CMTimeGetSeconds(time) / totalSeconds
489	        lock.lock()
490	        progressValue = min(max(fraction, progressValue), 1)
491	        lock.unlock()
492	    }
493	
494	    /// Main thread, once every input has marked itself finished — each reader
495	    /// already cancelled by its own pump on a stop (#378): the writer is
496	    /// cancelled or finished.
497	    private func allInputsFinished() {
498	        lock.lock()
499	        let error = failure
500	        let cancelled = cancelRequested
501	        lock.unlock()
502	        if fault != nil {
503	            let state = { (reader: AVAssetReader?) in
504	                reader.map { "\($0.status.rawValue)" } ?? "none"
505	            }
506	            let shared = audioReader != nil && audioReader === videoReader ? " (one reader)" : ""
507	            fault?.note(
508	                "readers: video \(state(videoReader)), audio \(state(audioReader))" + shared)
509	        }
510	        encodePump?.close()
511	        if let error = error {
512	            writer.cancelWriting()
513	            report(.failure(error))
514	            return
515	        }
516	        if cancelled {
517	            // `cancelWriting` deletes the part-written file itself, which is
518	            // the same outcome the progress sheet arranges for a cancel.
519	            writer.cancelWriting()
520	            report(.failure(Exporter.ExportError.cancelled))
521	            return
522	        }
523	        writer.finishWriting { [weak self] in
524	            // AVFoundation calls this on a queue of its own.
525	            DispatchQueue.main.async { self?.writingFinished() }
526	        }
527	    }
528	
529	    private func writingFinished() {
530	        lock.lock()
531	        let cancelled = cancelRequested
532	        lock.unlock()
533	        // A cancel that lands while the container is being closed still means
534	        // "I do not want this file": the sheet removes the destination on a
535	        // cancelled result, and a file the user cancelled out of is not one to
536	        // hand back because the timing was unlucky.
537	        guard !cancelled else {
538	            report(.failure(Exporter.ExportError.cancelled))
539	            return
540	        }
541	        guard writer.status == .completed else {
542	            report(
543	                .failure(
544	                    writer.error
545	                        ?? Exporter.ExportError.failed("The export stopped before it finished.")))
546	            return
547	        }
548	        // The `av01` brand AVAssetWriter leaves out (spec §11 CX-12 (4)).
549	        if encodePump != nil {
550	            do {
551	                try ExportAV1Track.brandFile(destination)
552	            } catch {
553	                report(.failure(error))
554	                return
555	            }
556	        }
557	        lock.lock()
558	        progressValue = 1
559	        lock.unlock()
560	        report(.success(destination))
561	    }
562	
563	    /// The one exit, main thread, at most once.
564	    private func report(_ result: Result<URL, any Error>) {
565	        guard let completion = completion else { return }
566	        self.completion = nil
567	        completion(result)
568	    }
569	}

1	// Codec export C6a (spec §11 CX-18) — the Export Queue's memory limit on bundled-encoder
     2	// jobs and the sheet's time estimate, in process. `encoder_limit_proof.py` builds it as
     3	// `main.swift` over every file in `app/Sources` but the app's own `main.swift`, on
     4	// `swift_build.py`'s line, beside `Blank.mp4`, `Fonts` and a `default.metallib` of
     5	// `Compositor.metal` and `ExportI010.metal`, and runs it:
     6	//
     7	//   encoder_limit_probe <AV.mov> <out folder> <answer.json>
     8	//
     9	// No app and no instance: the two live projects are built here from AV.mov, as
    10	// `webm_readers_probe.swift` builds A1's — A1 (640 × 360, 30 fps, AV.mov from 0 under a
    11	// two-second text clip) and W9 (1920 × 1080, AV.mov 24 times end to end at scale 3).
    12	//
    13	// The answer is RAW: the tables (P0), what the rule and the estimate answered (R, E), and
    14	// what the live queue did (Q), each event stamped with a sequence number. The proof
    15	// computes every expected value from P0's tables in its own arithmetic and scores the rows.
    16	import AVFoundation
    17	import AppKit
    18	import Foundation
    19	
    20	DecoderSupport.enable()
    21	NSApplication.shared.setActivationPolicy(.prohibited)
    22	
    23	let arguments = CommandLine.arguments
    24	guard arguments.count == 4 else {
    25	    print("usage: encoder_limit_probe <AV.mov> <out folder> <answer.json>")
    26	    exit(2)
    27	}
    28	let media = URL(fileURLWithPath: arguments[1])
    29	let outFolder = URL(fileURLWithPath: arguments[2], isDirectory: true)
    30	let answerURL = URL(fileURLWithPath: arguments[3])
    31	try? FileManager.default.createDirectory(at: outFolder, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
    32	
    33	let binaryDirectory = URL(fileURLWithPath: arguments[0]).deletingLastPathComponent()
    34	    .standardizedFileURL
    35	let fontsDirectory = binaryDirectory.appendingPathComponent("Fonts")
    36	for name in (try? FileManager.default.contentsOfDirectory(atPath: fontsDirectory.path)) ?? []
    37	where name.hasSuffix(".ttf") || name.hasSuffix(".otf") {
    38	    CTFontManagerRegisterFontsForURL(
    39	        fontsDirectory.appendingPathComponent(name) as CFURL, .process, nil)
    40	}
    41	
    42	var answer: [String: Any] = [:]
    43	func finish() -> Never {
    44	    let data = (try? JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: answer, options: [.sortedKeys]))
    45	        ?? Data("{}".utf8)
    46	    try? data.write(to: answerURL)
    47	    exit(0)
    48	}
    49	
    50	struct ProbeError: Error, CustomStringConvertible {
    51	    let description: String
    52	    init(_ d: String) { description = d }
    53	}
    54	
    55	// MARK: - P0: the tables
    56	
    57	func keyJSON(_ key: ExportEncoderKey) -> [String: Any] {
    58	    ["preset": key.preset, "speed": key.speed?.rawValue ?? NSNull(), "bits": key.bits]
    59	}
    60	func figureJSON(_ f: ExportEncoderFigure) -> [String: Any] {
    61	    ["at1080": f.at1080, "at2160": f.at2160, "source": f.source]
    62	}
    63	answer["pixels1080"] = ExportEncoderCosts.pixels1080
    64	answer["pixels2160"] = ExportEncoderCosts.pixels2160
    65	answer["memory"] = ExportEncoderCosts.memory.map { key, figure in
    66	    ["key": keyJSON(key), "figure": figureJSON(figure)]
    67	}
    68	answer["time"] = ExportEncoderCosts.time.map { key, entry in
    69	    ["key": keyJSON(key), "perFrame": figureJSON(entry.perFrame),
    70	     "setupSeconds": entry.setupSeconds]
    71	}
    72	
    73	// MARK: - Synthetic settings
    74	
    75	/// Settings as the core would answer them for a row, decoded through the app's own type.
    76	func settings(
    77	    preset: String, writer: String?, speed: EncoderSpeed? = nil, color: String? = nil,
    78	    width: Int, height: Int, frames: Int = 300, fps: [Int] = [30, 1]
    79	) -> ExportSettings {
    80	    var object: [String: Any] = [
    81	        "preset": preset, "container": "mp4", "codec": preset, "width": width,
    82	        "height": height, "fps": fps,
    83	        "range": ["start": 0, "duration": frames * Int(Fps.thirty.frameDuration)],
    84	    ]
    85	    if let writer { object["writer"] = writer }
    86	    if let speed { object["encoder_speed"] = speed.rawValue }
    87	    if let color { object["color"] = color }
    88	    let data = try! JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: object)
    89	    return ReelJSON.decode(ExportSettings.self, from: String(decoding: data, as: UTF8.self))!
    90	}
    91	
    92	/// One settings per measured key, by the proof's name for it.
    93	func keyed(width: Int, height: Int, frames: Int = 300) -> [(String, ExportSettings)] {
    94	    var out: [(String, ExportSettings)] = []
    95	    for preset in ["av1", "av1_webm"] {
    96	        for speed in EncoderSpeed.allCases {
    97	            out.append(("\(preset):\(speed.rawValue)", settings(
    98	                preset: preset, writer: "svt_av1", speed: speed, width: width, height: height,
    99	                frames: frames)))
   100	        }
   101	    }
   102	    out.append(("vp9_webm:sdr", settings(
   103	        preset: "vp9_webm", writer: "libvpx", width: width, height: height, frames: frames)))
   104	    out.append(("vp9_webm:hlg", settings(
   105	        preset: "vp9_webm", writer: "libvpx", color: "hlg", width: width, height: height,
   106	        frames: frames)))
   107	    out.append(("vp9_alpha_webm", settings(
   108	        preset: "vp9_alpha_webm", writer: "libvpx", width: width, height: height,
   109	        frames: frames)))
   110	    return out
   111	}

   113	// MARK: - R: the rule
   114	
   115	let gib: UInt64 = 1 << 30
   116	var r1: [[String: Any]] = []
   117	for physical in [16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128] {
   118	    let ledger = ExportEncoderLedger(physicalMemory: UInt64(physical) * gib)
   119	    for (width, height) in [(1920, 1080), (3840, 2160)] {
   120	        for (name, s) in keyed(width: width, height: height) {
   121	            let fresh = ExportEncoderLedger(physicalMemory: UInt64(physical) * gib)
   122	            var admitted = 0
   123	            while fresh.admits(s), admitted < 1000 {
   124	                _ = fresh.begin(s)
   125	                admitted += 1
   126	            }
   127	            r1.append([
   128	                "physicalGiB": physical, "budget": ledger.budget, "key": name,
   129	                "width": width, "height": height,
   130	                "cost": ExportEncoderCosts.memoryBytes(for: s, budget: ledger.budget),
   131	                "admitted": admitted,
   132	            ])
   133	        }
   134	    }
   135	}
   136	answer["r1"] = r1
   137	
   138	do {
   139	    let ledger = ExportEncoderLedger(physicalMemory: 64 * gib)
   140	    // A writer row with no entry: every real row is measured (codec-export C5's fix pass
   141	    // measured vp9_alpha_webm), so the rule is read on a synthetic one.
   142	    let alpha = settings(preset: "unmeasured_webm", writer: "libvpx", width: 1920, height: 1080)
   143	    let av1 = settings(preset: "av1", writer: "svt_av1", speed: .faster, width: 640, height: 360)
   144	    let firstAlpha = ledger.admits(alpha)
   145	    let alphaToken = ledger.begin(alpha)
   146	    let secondAlpha = ledger.admits(alpha)
   147	    let av1Beside = ledger.admits(av1)
   148	    let alphaCost = ExportEncoderCosts.memoryBytes(for: alpha, budget: ledger.budget)
   149	    ledger.end(alphaToken)
   150	    let av1Token = ledger.begin(av1)
   151	    let alphaBesideAV1 = ledger.admits(alpha)
   152	    ledger.end(av1Token)
   153	    answer["r2"] = [
   154	        "budget": ledger.budget, "alphaCost": alphaCost, "firstAdmitted": firstAlpha,
   155	        "secondAdmitted": secondAlpha, "av1BesideAlpha": av1Beside,
   156	        "alphaBesideAV1": alphaBesideAV1, "idle": ledger.runningCosts.isEmpty,
   157	    ]
   158	
   159	    let h264 = settings(preset: "h264", writer: nil, width: 3840, height: 2160)
   160	    let full = ExportEncoderLedger(physicalMemory: 16 * gib)
   161	    let held = full.begin(alpha)
   162	    let before = full.runningCosts
   163	    let h264Token = full.begin(h264)
   164	    answer["r3"] = [
   165	        "token": h264Token.map { NSNumber(value: $0) } ?? NSNull(),
   166	        "admittedBesideFull": full.admits(h264),
   167	        "costsUnchanged": full.runningCosts == before,
   168	        "cost": ExportEncoderCosts.memoryBytes(for: h264, budget: full.budget),
   169	        "key": ExportEncoderKey(settings: h264) == nil,
   170	    ]
   171	    full.end(held)
   172	}
   173	
   174	// MARK: - E: the estimate
   175	
   176	var e1: [[String: Any]] = []
   177	for (width, height) in [(1280, 720), (1920, 1080), (2560, 1440), (3840, 2160), (7680, 4320)] {
   178	    for frames in [150, 300, 1800] {
   179	        for (name, s) in keyed(width: width, height: height, frames: frames) {
   180	            e1.append([
   181	                "key": name, "width": width, "height": height, "frames": frames,
   182	                "seconds": ExportEncoderCosts.estimatedSeconds(for: s) ?? NSNull(),
   183	                "line": ExportEncoderCosts.sheetLine(for: s) ?? NSNull(),
   184	            ])
   185	        }
   186	    }
   187	}
   188	answer["e1"] = e1
   189	answer["e2"] = [0.4, 2.4, 7.4, 57.4, 59.9, 60, 89, 90, 3569, 3570, 3600, 5399, 5400].map {
   190	    ["seconds": $0, "text": ExportEncoderCosts.estimateText(seconds: $0)]
   191	}
   192	let h264Settings = settings(preset: "h264", writer: nil, width: 1920, height: 1080)
   193	// A measured key at a rate that cannot be stepped: no frame count, so no estimate.
   194	let unsteppedSettings = settings(
   195	    preset: "av1", writer: "svt_av1", speed: .balanced, width: 1920, height: 1080,
   196	    fps: [0, 1])
   197	answer["e3"] = [
   198	    "line": ExportEncoderCosts.sheetLine(for: h264Settings).map { $0 as Any } ?? NSNull(),
   199	    "seconds": ExportEncoderCosts.estimatedSeconds(for: h264Settings).map { $0 as Any }
   200	        ?? NSNull(),
   201	    "unsteppedFrames": unsteppedSettings.sequenceFrameCount.map { $0 as Any } ?? NSNull(),
   202	    "unsteppedLine": ExportEncoderCosts.sheetLine(for: unsteppedSettings).map { $0 as Any }
   203	        ?? NSNull(),
   204	    "unsteppedSeconds": ExportEncoderCosts.estimatedSeconds(for: unsteppedSettings)
   205	        .map { $0 as Any } ?? NSNull(),
   206	] as [String: Any]
   207	
   208	// MARK: - The live projects
   209	
   210	func apply(_ project: ReelProject, _ op: ReelOp) throws -> ReelProject {
   211	    switch try project.applying([op]) {
   212	    case .applied(let next): return next
   213	    case .identity: return project

   308	/// What the shared queue and ledger did during a live row: every job's state at each
   309	/// change, stamped by a sequence number, and the sequence at which the sheet was first
   310	/// seen finished (checked at every change and every spin, before the jobs are read).
   311	final class Watch {
   312	    let queue = ExportQueueController.shared
   313	    var seq = 0
   314	    var sheet: ExportProgressSheetController?
   315	    var sheetFinishedAt: Int?
   316	    var firstSeen: [String: Int] = [:]   // "<id>:<state>" → seq
   317	    var ledgerCosts: [[UInt64]] = []
   318	    var observers: [NSObjectProtocol] = []
   319	
   320	    init() {
   321	        observers.append(NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
   322	            forName: ExportQueueController.didChangeNotification, object: queue, queue: nil
   323	        ) { [unowned self] _ in self.tick() })
   324	        observers.append(NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
   325	            forName: ExportEncoderLedger.didChangeNotification,
   326	            object: ExportEncoderLedger.shared, queue: nil
   327	        ) { [unowned self] _ in
   328	            self.ledgerCosts.append(ExportEncoderLedger.shared.runningCosts)
   329	            self.tick()
   330	        })
   331	    }
   332	
   333	    func tick() {
   334	        seq += 1
   335	        if sheetFinishedAt == nil, let sheet, sheetFinished(sheet) { sheetFinishedAt = seq }
   336	        for job in queue.jobs {
   337	            let key = "\(job.id):\(job.state.rawValue)"
   338	            if firstSeen[key] == nil { firstSeen[key] = seq }
   339	        }
   340	    }
   341	
   342	    func at(_ id: UInt64, _ state: ExportQueueController.State) -> Any {
   343	        firstSeen["\(id):\(state.rawValue)"].map { $0 as Any } ?? NSNull()
   344	    }
   345	
   346	    func job(_ id: UInt64) -> [String: Any] {
   347	        let job = queue.job(id)
   348	        return [
   349	            "state": job?.state.rawValue ?? "missing", "message": job?.message ?? NSNull(),
   350	            "waiting": at(id, .waiting), "running": at(id, .running),
   351	            "completed": at(id, .completed), "failed": at(id, .failed),
   352	        ]
   353	    }
   354	
   355	    func stop() { observers.forEach(NotificationCenter.default.removeObserver) }
   356	}

   448	    let z = queue.enqueue(project: empty, urls: [:], settings: emptySettings,

   212	    case .applied(let next): return next
   213	    case .identity: return project
   214	    case .refused(let refusal): throw ProbeError("\(op.name) was refused: \(refusal.reason)")

   216	}

   218	/// The project with AV.mov in its media, on a canvas of `width` × `height` at 30 fps.
   219	func withMedia(width: Int, height: Int) throws -> (ReelProject, UInt32) {
   220	    var project = try apply(
   221	        ProjectDocument().project, .setCanvas(width: width, height: height, fps: Fps.thirty))
   222	    let asset = AVURLAsset(url: media)
   223	    let video = asset.tracks(withMediaType: .video).first
   224	    let size = video?.naturalSize ?? .zero
   225	    let id = project.snapshot.nextId

   227	        path: media.path, kind: .video, duration: CompositionBuilder.ticks(asset.duration),
   228	        width: Int(size.width), height: Int(size.height), fps: Fps.thirty,
   229	        hasVideo: video != nil, hasAudio: !asset.tracks(withMediaType: .audio).isEmpty)))

   231	}

   234	    var (project, id) = try withMedia(width: 640, height: 360)

   236	    project = try apply(project, .addClip(track: track, media: id, at: 0))
   237	    project = try apply(project, .addTrack(index: project.snapshot.tracks.count, name: "Titles"))
   238	    guard let titles = project.snapshot.tracks.last?.id else { throw ProbeError("no titles") }
   239	    return try apply(project, .addTextClip(
   240	        track: titles, at: 0, duration: 2 * ReelTime.perSecond, text: TextPatch(content: "AV1")))

   249	    }

   278	}
